about: The board cards' dioramas (BACKLOG.md 'The site itself: Blender dioramas'). `style` is the style sheet every card shares and common.py's diorama section builds from: the render size (2640 by 1600, the 33:20 promote-previews.mjs crops both outputs from), the plinth (its top, `top` metres wide by deep, is the plane Z = 0), the camera, the three lights and the backdrop. `frame` is what dioramas.mjs --rendered holds each render to: everything that is not backdrop inside `safe` (x0, y0, x1, y1 as fractions of the frame from its top left; y1 keeps it above the og card's crop, which loses the bottom 13%), spanning at least `minWidth` of the frame, with a pixel counted as backdrop when it is within `tolerance` (0-255, per channel) of its row's own colour at the frame's left edge, read as the median of the row's pixels 1 to 5, with the frame's outermost pixel ring left unread (#853). `machine` is the one machine every render in the set comes from (a lit render's pixels differ between machines). Each card is named as its preview is (index.html data-preview, promote-previews.mjs KNOWN) and lists what stands on its plinth: `ground` recolours the plinth top, `shapes` are built for the card (patch: a flat prism over a polygon, which may take `emit`; wall; pine; post; window; and for a game with no Blender pipeline the five plain solids of #850: block, prism, ball, dots and ring), any of them repeated `count` times `step` apart, and `place` imports the game's own .glb files from `project`, at a point on the plinth top, `z` above it, `rot` degrees about Z and `scale`, repeated `count` times `step` apart. A game that ships no .glb has `build` instead (#848): `calls` run the game's own sprite script (`build`, from `project`, with its project's common.py) one function or BUILDERS frame at a time, [name, arg ...] with {rng: n} for the project's seeded generator, {spec: true} for its spec and {palette: key} for a colour from the game's own table; what they build stands under one empty placed like `place`, its unlit sprite materials made lit in the same colours, `colours` recolours a material by name (Absalom's heir is a tint mask; Corner & Kettle's liquid is white until the game tints it; Orbital's star takes its own dark stop, #851) and `glow` gives one an emission strength in its own colour. A `wall` may take `z` to stand on something. Castle Conundrum is out of scope (#491).
machine: Devon's Windows machine: RTX 3070 Ti, Blender 5.2.2 LTS (Steam), Cycles on OptiX
